entities.summary: Ivan Fyodorov was a Russian navigator and commanding officer of the expedition to northern Alaska in 1732, whose successful voyage marked a significant milestone in the exploration of the region and expanded Russia's territorial claims in North America. The expedition, commissioned by Peter the Great, aimed to establish a Russian presence in the New World and assert the empire's dominance over the Pacific Ocean. Ivan Fyodorov's leadership and navigational skills played a crucial role in the expedition's success, as he successfully navigated the treacherous waters of the Bering Strait and established a temporary Russian settlement at Cape Prince of Wales. This achievement marked the beginning of a long history of Russian exploration and settlement in Alaska, which would eventually lead to the establishment of the Russian-American Company and the transfer of Alaska to the United States in 1867. Ivan Fyodorov's legacy as a pioneering explorer and navigator has been recognized in Russia and beyond, with his name becoming synonymous with bravery, skill, and discovery in the annals of Russian history.
